sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text: Cultists are a faction in Escape from Tarkov.

sections.heading: Biography
sections.text: Little is known about the Witnesses of the Arrival, the hooded figures conducting rituals and gathering in marked rooms at night. Their goals and beliefs remain a mystery even after years of activity in Tarkov.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- Cultist's footsteps have reduced volume.
- Cultists have a body temperature of 28 °C, making them harder to detect with thermal vision sights than other entities.
- Killing Cultists as a Scav does not carry any penalties towards your Scav karma.
- The Cultist priest and his 2-4 followers have different health values than PMCs and Scavs.

sections.heading: Quests
sections.text:
- 1 Cultist priest needs to be killed for the quest Broadcast - Part 5.
- 1 Cultist priest needs to be killed for the story chapter They Are Already Here.
- 3 Cultists need to be killed for the quest Hell on Earth - Part 2.
- 1 cultist knife needs to be obtained for the quest Broadcast - Part 5.
- 4 cultist knives needs to be obtained for the quest Small Business - Part 3.
- 12 cultist knives need to be obtained for the quest Night Sweep.
- 5 Cultists need to be killed for the quest New Beginning (Prestige 6).

sections.heading: Location
sections.text: Cultists appear between 22:00 and 7:00. They can be found on the following locations:

sections.heading: Night Factory
sections.text: Cultist priest with 2-3 warriors: Due to the small size of the location they have to be expected everywhere.

sections.heading: Customs
sections.text: Cultist priest with 4 warriors: In the construction area around the Scav base and the laboratory.

- Near the checkpoint west of the sawmill

sections.heading: Behavior
sections.text:
Cultists will lay prone in groups of 3-5 (depending on the map) with knives out waiting to ambush the player. Once a player gets close enough to a cultist warrior, it will stand up and chase the player in an attempt to stab them with either normal knives, or a poisoned cultist knife if the possess it. After the cultist has stabbed the player, they may attempt to back off into the shadows to fire upon them. If fired upon, the cultist warriors will begin to return fire upon the player with their weapons and grenades.

Cultist warriors will ignore scavs, scav guards, bosses, and scav players until that have been harmed. Cultist priests will attempt to run to cover whenever a player comes too close to their current location if any warriors are still alive. In the case that all warriors are dead and a player gets too close, the priest will stand up from his position and drop a grenade at his feet. The priest will make no attempt to flee from this grenade, and his death will not count towards the player unless he is killed before it detonates. In the rare case that this attempt fails, he will open fire upon the player.

Cultist warriors prefer to ambush players and will stay extremely well hidden. It is highly important that players locate the cultists and regain control of the fight. Cultists have almost no thermal signature and are very difficult to spot due to a preference to lay prone in bushes and tall grass. The cultists almost always have suppressors and prefer to stick to cover once engaged.

Cultists spawn with a range of gear from little armor to class 6, as well as high penetration ammo. They are known to throw grenades in very rare cases. They only wear face protection in rare cases, so headshots are a preferred method to deal with them.

If stabbed by the Cultist knife, players will be inflicted with the Unknown toxin debuff, which deals gradual damage over time (140 HP/minute) and causes pain. The toxin can be cured by the xTG-12 or Perfotoran injectors. Otherwise, the player must extract from the raid or they will run out of medication and die.

When it's time for them to disappear, they stand up from their ambush spots and despawn. Dead Cultists remain in their locations.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
- The cultist priest's name is always Zhrets (| zhrɛts |) which, in Russian, denotes a priest that performs sacrifices and doesn't serve the Christian God.
- Cultist warrior names are hidden, instead appearing as "Sektant", a loose translation of "Cultist" to Russian.
  - Zryachiy's followers also show up as "Sektant" in the kill list, but are not the exact same AI type as regular Cultists, and therefore do not count for Cultist related quests or achievements.
